task.description: Produce the design artefact for REQ-230 (entity query DSL security half): closed operator enum, per-tenant field allowlist with typed-column-vs-JSONB precedence, and a parameterised SQL compiler.

result.note: Design doc written to lib/letflow/design/req230-entity-query-dsl-compiler.md (742 lines). Operator enum explicitly stated as CODE-DESIGNER's own construction (R-Co source unreachable, no QRY-01..05 definition found anywhere accessible in this repo) -- not presented as transcribed: closed filter_op() set (:eq, :neq, :gt, :gte, :lt, :lte, :in, :not_in, :contains, :starts_with, :is_null, :is_not_null) plus separate sort_dir(), modeled on the existing Letflow.Engine.Expr.cmp_op() closed-union idiom, each operator restricted to meaningful field types. Allowlist precedence rule: a field backed by a real typed column on entity_record_latest always wins over the same name found only as a JSONB key in field_values; only queried: true entity-definition fields are ever allowlisted from the JSONB side (structurally excludes :json-typed fields, since the existing validator already forbids :json + queried: true). Compiler's fragment/1 discipline: per-field_type() cast fragments are each a compile-time-literal string selected via pattern-matched dispatch, never assembled at runtime; both the JSONB key name and the comparison value are bound as separate ^-parameters -- stronger than AC4 requires, since it parameterizes the key too, not just the value. IMPORTANT FOR VALIDATOR: self-check noted a few short illustrative inline backtick snippets in prose (an illustrative case arm, an Enum.reduce shape) -- scrutinize these carefully to confirm they are genuinely short inert illustrations inside sentences (matching req229's own precedent style), not disguised executable code blocks.
